what_happened: Re-measurement found the dispatch's own at-creation figure (22 resolve_candidate callers) undercounted the true population by more than half: a third, grep-invisible shape (inline CANDIDATES-array for-loop, 38 suites) implements the identical deploy-tree-first/source-store-fallback pattern without ever naming a function resolve_candidate. True family size is 70 of 144 scripts/tests/*.sh suites, not 22/60/119 nor the stale doc's 41/73.

Direct inspection of common_test_resolve_candidate call sites found the implicit resolution order is NOT uniformly deploy-tree-first even today: test-gate-out-derived-staleness.sh and test-install-uninstall-extension.sh both pass the source-store candidate first. Confirms the preference is caller-specific and currently undeclared/unaudited, exactly the defect the dispatch describes -- not a single uniform default that merely needs documenting.

Plan-time territory scan found scripts/tests/test-lint-dead-command-recommendations.sh is both in this task's 70-suite migration family (Group A) and in concurrent sibling task 512's declared file_scope for this same cycle. Declared it in Phase 3's Files to modify so the admission gate serializes the two tasks rather than silently excluding the file, with a re-read-before-edit step and an allowlist-deferral contingency in Rollback.

Every population figure in the research report (144 total suites, 70 family, 20 shared-helper / 12 local-duplicate / 38 inline-loop, 3 deployed-only) reproduced byte-for-byte at plan-authoring time from the report's own Appendix commands, so the plan's phase batching could be built on measured file lists instead of estimates. The report's reproducible-commands appendix is what made that cheap.

Direct inspection of Group B (local-duplicate) suite test-force-phases.sh found it does NOT define a function literally named resolve_candidate() (the grep -Fl 'resolve_candidate()' hit was from a header comment referencing a SIBLING suite's function). It instead defines its own resolve_inverted(), deliberately inverted to source-store-first for 4 (later 5, including orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh) specific files under test, with every other dependency staying deploy-tree-first. This is a THIRD confirmed non-default-order caller beyond the two named in research (test-gate-out-derived-staleness.sh, test-install-uninstall-extension.sh), and its migration in Phase 4 must preserve the per-file split (some deps mode=source-store, others mode=deploy-tree-first) rather than assuming the whole file moves to one mode.

Phase 2 verification criterion 'test-manifest-scripts-sync.sh exits 0' is blocked by a PRE-EXISTING, out-of-scope gap: manifest.json already carried an uncommitted 'lib/gate-store-fixture-lib.sh' provides.scripts declaration (and the file itself exists untracked on disk) from a concurrent/prior session before this dispatch began -- confirmed via git diff isolation (that hunk is disjoint from my own two manifest.json hunks). I staged only my own two manifest.json hunks (lint/lint-subject-resolution-declaration.sh, tests/test-lint-subject-resolution-declaration.sh) via a hand-built partial patch (git apply --cached) rather than a whole-file git add, to avoid sweeping the sibling's uncommitted work into this task's commit. test-manifest-scripts-sync.sh still reports 1 absent-but-declared gap for the sibling's file; this is not caused by and not fixed by this task.

Near-miss: committing manifest.json via git commit -- <pathspec> (intending to commit only an already git-apply --cached-staged partial patch) actually takes the WORKING-TREE content for the named path, not just the index -- it swept a concurrent sibling's unrelated, unstaged, uncommitted lib/gate-store-fixture-lib.sh manifest.json line into the commit. Caught immediately via git show --stat. Corrected with a second, narrow commit removing that one line from HEAD, then restored the sibling's line back into the working tree uncommitted (via Edit, no git add) so their in-progress work is preserved exactly as found rather than erased. Verified via test-manifest-scripts-sync.sh and git status that the final state matches the original pre-dispatch condition plus this task's own two manifest.json entries correctly committed.
